title: `/auth/me/permissions` and `/me/apps` re-implement permission-set resolution instead of calling the plugin's service — the copy that produced #7608 (and #7270, #7560)
body:
Restart-when: `git grep -c "resolvePermissionSetsForContext" "$(git tag --sort=-creatordate | grep '^@objectstack/spec@' | head -1)" -- packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts` returns non-zero — i.e. the newest cut @objectstack/spec release carries the contract method, so plugin-hono-server may assume it and drop the `Partial<ISecurityService>` fallback.

Filed as a **finding** while implementing #7608 (PR #7615), which asked whether these endpoints should stop re-implementing this resolution at all. Measured there and deliberately not folded in; recording the measurement so the decision is on file rather than an unexamined copy.

## The drift surface

`packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/current-user-endpoints.ts` resolves the caller's permission sets itself, twice — once for the `/auth/me/permissions` object/field surface and once for the `/me/apps` capability + tab surface. `SecurityPlugin.resolvePermissionSetsForContext` resolves the same thing for the data plane. That is **one rule with three copies**, and it has now drifted twice in the way that shape always drifts:

- **#7608** — the plugin applied the ADR-0090 D5 baseline additively; both endpoints kept the fallback **cliff** (`resolved.length === 0 && …`), so a member who received their first grant lost the baseline on the UI plane while keeping it on the data plane. Measured effect: receiving a grant took a member from **2 apps to 1** on `/me/apps`.
- **#7555 / PR #7605** — an app-declared `isDefault` set **displaced** `member_default` here rather than composing with it, for the same reason: the composition lived in the plugin and the endpoints re-derived it.
- **#6334** — the same file's grant aggregation missed `sys_user_position` / `sys_position_permission_set` entirely; closed by delegating to `resolveUserAuthzGrants`. That delegation is the precedent this card is asking to extend one step further.

PR #7615 shrank the surface where it was cheap — the rule is now one named `effectivePermissionSetNames` helper documented against the plugin's method by name — but the copy itself is still there.

## What a real de-duplication costs (measured, not estimated)

The published `ISecurityService` (`packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts`) exposes `resolvePermissionSetNames(context)`, returning **names only**. Both handlers need the full resolved sets — `objects`, `fields`, `systemPermissions`, `tabPermissions` — for their merges, so today's contract cannot serve them. Extending it means:

- `packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts` — a new `resolvePermissionSetsForContext`-shaped method, plus `security-service.test.ts`, whose contract test asserts an **exhaustive** method list;
- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts` — the method is `private` today; expose it on the registered service literal;
- `current-user-endpoints.ts` — the call site.

**3 packages, ~5 files.**

Two things make it a net **addition** rather than a removal, which is why it did not ride on the #7608 fix:

1. **The contract mandates feature-detection.** Consumers resolve the service as `Partial<ISecurityService>` by design, so this file must keep the local resolution as the fallback for a SecurityPlugin too old to carry the method — leaving the copy **plus** the delegation **plus** a branch between them, until that fallback can be dropped. De-duplication that adds a third path is not de-duplication yet.
2. **The two are not the same resolution.** The plugin resolves through `this.metadata` / `this.bootstrapPermissionSets` / `this.dbLoader`; these endpoints pass their own loaders, and `/me/apps` deliberately projects a **narrower** column set (`name` + `systemPermissions` + `tabPermissions`) than `/auth/me/permissions` does. Delegating changes which columns load on both surfaces — a behaviour change wanting its own before/after measurement, not a refactor.

A third constraint worth stating so it is not rediscovered: `plugin-hono-server` must **not** take a runtime dependency on `plugin-security`, which is optional in the stacks these endpoints serve (the `!evaluator` degraded branches are exactly its absence). A service-locator call is structural and satisfies this; a package import would not.

## Suggested shape

Sequence it rather than doing it in one PR:

1. Add the method to `ISecurityService` + `plugin-security`, unused, so the contract exists and ships.
2. Once a floor version carrying it can be assumed, switch both call sites and delete the local resolution — measuring the column-projection change on `/me/apps` at that point, since that is the part with user-visible reach.

Until step 2, the copy stands knowingly. Worth noting the cost of *not* doing it is measurable: three separate cards so far, each found after the divergence reached a user rather than at author time.

## Related stale reference

`plugin-security`'s `resolveFallbackPermissionSets` doc-comment still describes "the second step `/auth/me/permissions` takes when a caller's own names resolve to nothing (`resolved.length === 0 && fallbackName`)". PR #7615 deletes that step. Comment-only, in a package outside that PR's file surface — fold it into whichever PR does the above, or a docs-only pass.
